title: Sierra Raises $1.75B at a $30B Valuation for AI Agents
dek: Bret Taylor's customer service AI startup doubled its value in six months.

facts.label: New round led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed

caption:
Six months. That's how long it took Sierra to double its valuation to $30 billion. 🚀

The customer service AI agent startup co-founded by Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor is raising $1.75 billion, led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Benchmark, Sequoia, GV and Tiger Global are all putting in more money too. Sierra says it has passed $400 million in annual recurring revenue, adding over $150 million in Q3 alone.

Sierra's AI agents handle returns, insurance claims and support for banks like JPMorganChase and Wells Fargo, plus insurers like Cigna. Its Ghostwriter tool builds and improves agents, and it charges per resolved issue instead of per seat.

We're tracking it at AI Parabellum: investors are betting customer service is where AI agents pay off first. The real test is whether those agents stay reliable at scale.

post_caption:
Next time a bank or insurer's chat agent solves your problem, it might be Sierra behind it. The Bret Taylor-backed startup just raised $1.75 billion at a $30 billion valuation, with revenue past $400 million a year.

Nearly half of Fortune 50 companies reportedly use it, and its outcome-based pricing means Sierra only earns when the agent actually fixes the issue. 💼
